push.title: W 4-2 vs Trotted On | You: 8.6 (2nd best match performance)
push.body:
BellyTb1, an 8.6. You played like someone who read the playbook twice and highlighted it.

THE GOOD
+ 25 passes. You were everywhere except the parking lot.
+ A brace against Trotted On, your 2nd straight match scoring. The goal was open and you walked right through the door.
+ Man of the Match, your 2nd for us. Leaders make the hard moments look easy.
+ Your 2nd best match performance: 8.6. That's the standard now.
+ Tackles won 2, up from your usual 0. You can build a whole match on that.

THE BAD
- Only 2 tackles attempted. Repeat after me: Second-ball awareness: after a header or clearance, be the first one to the loose ball.
- 68% passing (17 of 25). Let's try: Use the keeper and center-backs to reset. Recycling is how good teams find the gap. Habits beat highlights.
- No key passes from 25 passes. Fix it like this: Receive on the half-turn so your first touch can go forward. That's the whole secret.
- defensive work rate got you and tuxedo_slide. Communicate and pass runners off and track them into the box.

Back-garden drill: When the ball is lost, the nearest player presses and everyone else closes the passing lanes.

Between you and me, BellyTb1: Good passes are like good manners. Free, and people remember.

Take a bow. - Coach Lasso

push.title: W 4-2 vs Trotted On | You: 8.4 (worst match performance)
push.body:
tuxedo_slide, an 8.4 against Trotted On: your worst match performance. Let's make that a habit.

THE GOOD
+ A brace against Trotted On, your 2nd straight match scoring. Goals are like biscuits: always better shared, but I'll take this one.
+ 1 key pass. Selfless as a church potluck, and twice as filling.
+ You and BellyTb1 play like you've known each other since kindergarten.
+ Better match rating than any of their humans (8.4 vs their best 8.0). That right there is what good teammates do.
+ Fewest misplaced passes on the team (5). That's a habit, and habits win leagues.

THE BAD
- Only 1 tackle attempted. Try this: Know your runner before the cross comes in. A quick look over the shoulder saves a goal.
- defensive work rate snagged you and BellyTb1 both. Buddy system: pass runners off and track them into the box.

THE UGLY
! Pass accuracy 54% (6 of 11). That's the kind of thing that loses a team its spot in a division. One more thing: Scan before the ball gets to you - a quick shoulder check means you already know the pass before you need it.

Tonight's homework: Play in triangles - one or two touches, then move. The ball should do the running, not you.

tuxedo_slide, one more thing before you log off: Kindness costs nothing and wins locker rooms.

On to the next one. - Coach Lasso

push.title: W 4-2 vs Trotted On | You: 7.3 (3rd worst match performance)
push.body:
A 7.3, PhogsToffees. That's a speed bump, not a wall.

THE GOOD
+ 1 key pass. Making your teammates look good is the most generous thing in football.
+ You found BellyTb1 and BellyTb1 found the net. That's chemistry you can't buy at the store.
+ Better completed passes than any of their humans (23 vs their best 18). If the rest of the night was a storm, that was the lighthouse.
+ 4-2 against Trotted On. A win's a win, and this was a good one.

THE BAD
- No shots. Fundamentals: Get across your defender at the near post. Most close-range goals come from that first-post run.
- 72% passing (23 of 32). Best practice: Below about 72% the extra passes start costing us. Pick the simple option until the touch comes back. Keep it simple, keep it sweet.
- Your 3rd worst match performance (7.3). We'll get you back up the list.
- forcing passes showed up for you and BellyTb1. Talk it through and give each other short options.
- Tackles attempted 2, down from your usual 4. Note to self, from me to you.

Training-ground special: When you've got a clear look inside the box, pull the trigger. Hesitation lets defenders recover.

PhogsToffees, something I want you to sleep on: Taking on a challenge is a lot like riding a horse. Comfortable is overrated.

Trust the work. - Coach Lasso
